title: Improving Instructional Practice through Peer Observation and Feedback
extended_summary:
This paper asks what is known about peer observation and feedback as a way to improve instructional practice, especially in light of concerns that principal-led teacher evaluation is time-consuming, uneven in quality, and often insufficiently useful for instructional improvement. The authors frame peer coaching as a potentially more scalable and collaborative alternative to traditional administrator-centered supervision.

The paper is a systematic review of peer observation and feedback literature. The authors searched multiple education databases and, after screening, included 38 documents spanning 1984 to 2019. The reviewed studies covered pre-service and in-service teachers in a range of settings, with most studies qualitative or mixed-methods and only a small number using quantitative or quasi-experimental designs. The population contexts included elementary, secondary, and some higher-education teacher preparation settings across multiple countries.

The review concludes that peer observation and feedback is promising for instructional improvement, but the evidence base remains limited and uneven. Across studies, the most consistent reported benefits were increased collaboration, reflection, confidence, and some changes in instructional practice; however, the literature was small-scale, heterogeneous, and often lacked rigorous comparison groups. The authors emphasize that more piloting and stronger research are needed to identify which peer coaching models work best and under what conditions.

identified_tools.name: ITS (General)
identified_tools.description: An intelligent tutoring or coaching system that provides instructional support, feedback, or guidance to learners or teachers.
identified_tools.use_case: This paper does not study an AI tool; it is a systematic review of peer observation and feedback among human teachers, including peer coaching and reciprocal coaching models.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a systematic review of human peer observation and feedback, not an empirical evaluation of an AI tool. The paper synthesizes heterogeneous teacher coaching studies rather than testing a specific intervention with randomized or quasi-experimental design.
impact_tier_rationale: No AI tool or measurable AI-related intervention effect is reported. The review discusses potential instructional-improvement benefits of peer coaching, but these are human-to-human processes and not attributable to an AI system.
